problems.title: The odds theorem is conditional on generator-kernel calibration
claim: Equal distances imply equal Gaussian neighbor probabilities; the proof identifies that kernel with actual diffusion attribute probabilities.
analysis: Take \(z_1=(1,0),z_2=(-1,0),u=(0,1),\rho=1\). Equal squared distances \(2\) give kernel probabilities \((1/2,1/2)\). A separate generator can obey every attribute-specific prompt perfectly but generate attributes \((.9,.1)\) from the neutral prompt. A constant concept gives attribute–concept independence. This does not contradict a theorem that explicitly assumes the actual generator is the calibrated Gaussian kernel; it shows that neighbor selection and prompt compliance do not derive that premise.
result: Under the intended calibrated idealization the exponential-distance algebra is valid. Its application to learned diffusion remains a modeling assumption requiring qualification.
problems.impact_rationale: The countermodel excludes the strong calibration premise; this is an applicability clarification, not a refutation of the conditional idealized theorem.
problems.existing_correction_status: No applicable author correction was established in this inspection.

problems.title: Normalized centroid cosine changes the intended mean score
claim: The losses replace mean image cosine scores by cosine to an average image embedding, dropping the centroid norm.
analysis: For unit text \(u=(1,0)\), let attribute embeddings be \((.8,\pm.6)\) and \((.2,\pm\sqrt{.96})\), each equiprobable. Centroids \((.8,0)\) and \((.2,0)\) both have cosine \(1\), but squared distances to \(u\) are \(.04\) and \(.64\), giving calibrated odds \((.5744425,.4255575)\) at unit bandwidth. Generally \(E\cos(t,X)=t^T\mu\), whereas \(\cos(t,\mu)=t^T\mu/\|\mu\|\). Attribute-specific rotations preserve the example and give mean-score spread \(.3\) while centroid-cosine spread is zero. Algorithm 1’s raw dot product is valid counterevidence: actual implementation convention is unavailable.
result: The displayed cosine loss differs from the intended mean-score/unnormalized-distance target. This does not show the unreleased experiments used the wrong convention.
repair: Use raw centroid dot products for mean cosine. For distance-based odds, retain actual squared distances or explicitly redefine normalized representatives and calibrated model.
problems.impact_rationale: The exact formula discrepancy affects the stated objective, but raw-dot pseudocode may already implement the intended score and empirical fairness is not disproved.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: The embedding attention formula does not specify a foreground image
claim: Attention over image/text embeddings is described as a highlighted image fed back to the image encoder.
analysis: With one pooled image query and one pooled text key/value, the score has one entry, so softmax is \([1]\) and the output is the text value regardless of the image. Its shape is an embedding, not RGB pixels or a spatial mask. With token matrices, the output is a mixture of text values per image token; patch-grid selection, mask aggregation, normalization and upsampling are still needed. A hidden routine could supply them; visual examples do not uniquely define it.
result: The published operator is insufficient to reproduce the foreground module. Actual generated foreground images are not proved independent of input.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local specification gap; no full routine or practical ablation failure is established.
problems.existing_correction_status: No applicable author correction was established in this inspection.

problems.title: Spectral ordering needs a decreasing-power premise
claim: The proposition states a universal low-frequency recovery advantage and assigns attributes to late high-frequency recovery.
analysis: The derived SNR increment is \(\Delta_i(f)=K_iS(f)\), with \(K_i>0\). It decreases in frequency only if signal power does. A positive \(16\)-pixel signal \(x_j=3+\cos(2\pi j/16)/2+2\cos(8\pi j/16)\) has unitary powers \(S(1)=1,S(4)=16\). With cumulative noise values \(.1,.4,.2\) and unit expected noise power, increments are \(1/24\) and \(2/3\), reversing the unrestricted ordering. Dividing pixels by \(6\) fits \([0,1]\) without changing the ratio. A decreasing power-law model gives the claimed conditional ordering, but neither SNR nor frequency alone identifies semantic attribute timing.
result: The universal spectral/semantic explanation fails; the measured two-stage sampler can still work in its tested prompts.
repair: State the decreasing expected signal-power premise and restrict the result to the SNR surrogate; retain semantic timing as an empirical observation.
problems.impact_rationale: The failure concerns a broad explanatory rationale; the conditional power-law calculation and observed sampler utility survive.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

impact_rationale: Minor: objective/specification differences and overbroad interpretations are supported, with valid calibrated and raw-dot alternatives retained; core empirical fairness is not disproved.
